sources.title: The Alien Space of Science: Sampling Coherent but Cognitively Unavailable Research Directions
sources.rights: Original study notes from the owner-supplied paper; original PDF is not redistributed. Check artifact-specific terms before training.

notes.text: The Alien Space of Science: Sampling Coherent but Cognitively Unavailable Research Directions, arXiv:2603.01092v3, revised October 21, 2026, lists Alejandro H. Artiles, Martin Weiss, Levin Brinkmann, Iyad Rahwan, Bernhard Schölkopf, Christopher Pal, Hugo Larochelle, Anirudh Goyal and Nasim Rahaman.
notes.locator: PDF p.1, Title block and arXiv margin
notes.limitation: Do not replace version-specific author identity with an older bibliographic record or an inferred affiliation.

notes.text: The main study represents 16,068 LLM papers as combinations from 273 idea atoms. Papers are distilled into methodological units, then embedded, clustered and summarized into recurring concepts.
notes.locator: PDF p.4, 3.1 Representing Research Directions as Idea Atoms; PDF p.16,17, A.1 Data Collection and A.5 Atom Clustering
notes.limitation: The frozen temporal study uses a separately built 191-atom vocabulary; 273 is the main-corpus count. These are concepts from LLM literature, not a cybersecurity corpus.

notes.text: Coherence estimates whether atoms plausibly occur together in a paper. Availability estimates compatibility with published author repertoires; training separates the query atoms from the matched author input. This proxy is relative to the covered literature and does not measure a researcher’s mental state.
notes.locator: PDF p.4,5, 3.2 Modeling Scientific Coherence and 3.3 Modeling Cognitive Availability; PDF p.35, C.3 Held-Out-Author Test, Results
notes.limitation: Do not interpret publication patterns as exhaustive knowledge, inherent talent or a ranking of the paper’s nine authors.

notes.text: In the small blinded human idea study, Alien and Claude tied on mean overall quality at 4.025, rounded to 4.03. Ten raters with postgraduate degrees supplied 40 reviews over ten ideas per method.
notes.locator: PDF p.9, 5.4 Generated Ideas Remain Competitive in Quality, Human ratings; PDF p.43, E.1 Human Survey and Table 20
notes.limitation: Reviewer interpretation: equal sample means do not establish statistical equivalence or universal superiority. Batch baseline quality was imputed rather than rated separately (PDF page 8, Table 1).

notes.text: Frozen temporal validation ranks 1,143,135 triples from 191 pre-2025 atoms. At beta 0, the top 10,000 recover 762 of 2,424 targets, or 35.9 times the uniform-random expectation. At beta 0.4, they recover 40 of 1,411 strictly novel targets, or 3.24 times that group’s random expectation.
notes.locator: PDF p.7, 5.2 Frozen Pre-2025 Scores Recover 2025 Research Directions and Figure 3; PDF p.33,34, C.2 Frozen-Vocabulary Temporal Validation
notes.limitation: The factors refer to different target groups and beta settings. They measure recovery of atom combinations, not percentage accuracy, scientific productivity or vulnerability-discovery gains.

notes.text: The main generation comparison selects 300 triples from all 3,353,896 combinations of the 273-atom catalogue with beta 0.7. Its ranking blends standardized coherence with standardized unavailability; all compared methods use the same decoder and prompt for the downstream comparison.
notes.locator: PDF p.5,6, 3.4 Sampling the Alien Space and 4 Experimental Setup; PDF p.26,27,28, A.11 Sampling Parameters and A.11.1 Selecting beta
notes.limitation: Beta 0.7 is a main-experiment score weight, not a universally optimal setting, a resource budget, or the beta used for the 3.24-times temporal result.
